messages:
julia: Heads up — canary for redwood-v2-onboard (region us-west-2) showing ~30% tail latency regression after the model onboarding yesterday. Blocking rollout for now.
kevin: ugh. any quick numbers or dashboard links? can you paste the spike window?
julia: here — 02:14:00-02:40:00 UTC.  p99 jumped from 320ms -> 420ms. throughput stable. link: https://console.redwood/perf/dashboards/model-redwood-v2-canary
julia: ran a local profile on a representative trace. two odd things:
```
- kernel selection: previously used optimized_fused_ffn, now falling back to generic_cuda_gemm for many layers
- kv-cache hit rate: 93% -> 68% for this workload (same input distribution)
- avg seq len (after tokenization): 128 -> 210
```
kevin: avg seq len doubled — that smells like a tokenizer/config delta. was there a tokenization or tokenizer config change in the onboarding PRs?
matt: i remember #2345 touched tokenizer whitespace handling for that model checkpoint (to handle new special tokens). CI perf checks passed because our synthetic CI uses seq len 64, not a real-load distribution.
perf-bot: CI perf check flagged PR #2345 for small regressions on microbenchmarks but below alert threshold. (run-id: perf/2026-03-16-18:02)
kevin: ok bisect plan: (1) verify tokenizer token counts on sample corpus with old vs new checkpoint, (2) run kernel-selector trace for a sample convo, (3) bisect merges between yesterday and two days ago to find offending commit.
julia: i ran token counts on 10k samples; new tokenizer adds extra tokens for some punctuation sequences — histogram shifted. avg tokens/sample +65% for docs with URLs.
kevin: started git-bisect across merge window: suspect set = merges 2301..2350. Quick note: model config drift could change "max_positions"/padding behavior which affects kernel selection.
```
git bisect start --term-old old-good --term-new bad
git bisect good abcde123  # before onboarding
git bisect bad   9f8d7c6 # HEAD canary
# running candidate 2345 -> reproduces
```
kevin: bisect pointed to merge PR #2345 (tokenizer whitespace/special-token handling) as first bad.
matt: that PR also modified the tokenizer's `add_prefix_space` and changed default `truncate_longer_samples` behavior in config.json for that model.
rachel: is the fallback to generic_cuda_gemm coming from longer sequence lengths exceeding kernel tiling heuristic? maybe kernel selector uses sequence-length thresholds that the longer tokens now hit.
julia: traced kernel selector decisions — it switches to the slower path when sequence_len > 192 or when dynamic_memory_estimate > X. The tokenizer delta pushed many requests over that threshold.
kevin: repro locally by forcing tokenization legacy vs new: confirm p99 goes back down when using old tokenization. So root cause: tokenizer config drift -> longer sequences -> kernel path switch + higher KV cache churn (different alignments) -> perf regression.
perf-bot: Added ticket PERF-6622 linking to traces, bisect output, and config diff.
kevin: propose two immediate actions: (1) revert the tokenizer change in production (open PR), (2) add a short-term kernel-selector override to prefer optimized_fused_ffn for this model family until we fix tokenizer or update kernels.
rachel: opening revert PR now: PR #2401 (revert: PR #2345). marking as rollout-blocker.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for redwood-v2-onboard (reason: rollout-blocker by eng-runtime).
matt: after revert in canary, re-ran same load for 1h — p99 back to 325ms. KV cache hit rate back to ~92%. Good signal.
julia: moving forward: we need two follow-ups:
  - add a perf-presubmit that samples real seq length distributions (to catch tokenizer/seq regressions)
  - expand kernel-selector tests to exercise boundary seq lengths so small tokenizer deltas don't flip the path silently
kevin: also let's add an automated lint that checks tokenizer config changes (max_positions, add_prefix_space, truncation defaults) in model-onboard PRs and requires perf sign-off if changed.
julia: agreed. will create follow-up PRs for presubmit and lint rules.
kevin: thanks all — unblocking the rollout once revert lands. if anyone sees similar regressions in other models, ping this thread.
rachel: revert merged -> canary resumed -> monitoring shows stable latencies. closing the immediate blocker. :tada:
julia: adding retrospective notes to PERF-6622 and product onboarding checklist to avoid future config drift.
